failure_summary.description: Email-validation calls confused adjacent properties or used overlapping validators, both omitting distinct requested checks and adding redundant ones.
A call used a descriptive provider blurb instead of the listed tool identifier and placed an optional parameter in the required group.

patch.reasoning: The skill already specifies exact tool identifiers and schema groups, so repeating those rules is unlikely to help. A more explicit target-by-property checklist can address the recurring validation failures by separating requested diagnostic dimensions, selecting endpoints that actually measure them, and avoiding redundant checks.

edits.target: For each candidate, verify that its result fulfills the requested action for the right entity and scope: suggestions, checks of weaker properties, or unfiltered results do not substitute for a requested lookup, verification, or scoped result.
edits.content: For multi-facet verification tasks, make a target-by-property checklist before selecting tools. Distinguish the requested property (for example, address validity, mailbox deliverability, or disposable status) from the target level (an address versus a domain). A check for one property or level does not establish an adjacent one. Use a documented endpoint for each distinct requested property, allowing one endpoint to cover multiple properties only when its documentation supports them. Add another check for the same property only when the user requests an independent cross-check; do not interpret “comprehensive” as a reason to call every vaguely relevant validator.
